producer_report.summary:
I added optional `[models] planner_revision_model` and `planner_revision_effort`. After a critic revise or a mechanical plan-rule revision, the planner runs at those values, but only where each is set and not weaker than the planner's current value. Round 1 and a seeded first call are unchanged. The two keys are separate from `hard_producer_*`.

- **Config (`config.rs`):** `Models::planner_revision_setting` ranks effort by position in `EFFORT_LEVELS` and models by position in `producer_allowed`, now documented as weakest first. A part that would lower the value is ignored on its own. A model key outside `producer_allowed` gives the new `ConfigError::PlannerRevisionNotAllowed`. The membership check runs after the model-family check, so the existing family tests keep their errors. An out-of-range effort key is refused like the other effort keys. Both keys are cleared in `reading_inputs`, so stored readings stay valid.
- **Planner (`planning.rs`):** `planning_round` uses the revision setting when `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`. It sets `spec.effort` after `agent_spec`. The planner line now reads `planner    <model> · <effort> · …`, and the invocation record carries both values. Nothing in `planning.rs` reads `producer_setting` or `hard_producer_*`.
- **Repo config:** `athena.toml` sets `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `xhigh`, with a 'weakest first' note above `producer_allowed`. A hard reading goes from sonnet/high to sonnet/xhigh on revision calls (effort only). An unmarked reading planned for a fails-without criterion goes from the reader's pick at high to sonnet/xhigh, so a haiku planner moves up a model.
- **Tests:** four core tests drive `Athena::go` with a recording fake agent: critic revise, mechanical revision, weaker keys, and keys unset. Six config tests, and one `drain.rs` test that reads the repo's own `athena.toml`, cover the rest.
- **Docs:** a CHANGELOG entry gives the effective setting with and without the change for both planned cases. D179 is appended to `docs/decisions.md`. The OLY-A-11 mechanism text in `docs/spec.toml` names the revision setting.
- **Checks:** fmt, clippy, the policy scan, the mirrors test and the workspace test run all passed. I could not read the workspace run's output, so I cite only its exit code 0.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs drives Athena::go with the fake agent and a critic revise. It shows that the first planner invocation records the ordinary model and effort, and that the next one records planner_revision_model and planner_revision_effort. Run `cargo test -p athena-core` and cite the test name.
criteria_check.evidence: Test `a_critic_revise_sends_the_next_planner_call_at_the_revision_model_and_effort` in run/tests.rs drives Athena::go through `run_for_revision`. It asserts the planner calls are (haiku, high) then (sonnet, xhigh), that the Planner invocation records match, and that the planner lines carry the model and effort of each round. `cargo test -p athena-core a_critic_revise_sends` passed. The full workspace run also exited 0.

criteria_check.criterion: New tests show that a mechanical plan-rule revision also escalates the next planner call. They also show that a key weaker than the current planner model or effort is ignored, and that with both keys unset every round keeps the same model and effort. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria_check.evidence: In run/tests.rs: `planner_revision_applies_after_a_mechanical_plan_rule_revision` (no critic call between the two planner calls, second is sonnet/xhigh). `planner_revision_ignores_a_key_weaker_than_the_planner_setting` (haiku+medium keeps sonnet/high; haiku+xhigh gives sonnet/xhigh). `planner_revision_unset_keeps_every_round_at_the_same_setting` (4 planner calls across a mechanical pass and 3 rounds, all haiku/high). `cargo test -p athena-core planner_revision` passed 3 of 3, and the workspace run exited 0.

criteria_check.criterion: New config.rs unit tests show that the keys parse as optional, that a value outside the allowed lists is rejected, and that an existing config without the keys still loads. Run `cargo test -p athena-data`.
criteria_check.evidence: config.rs tests: `planner_revision_keys_are_optional_and_load_from_the_repository_config` (Some in the repo config, None once stripped, and the stripped config loads). `planner_revision_model_outside_producer_allowed_is_refused` (the verifier model and an unknown name give PlannerRevisionNotAllowed). The existing effort-key loop now includes planner_revision_effort and rejects 'turbo'. Also `planner_revision_setting_uses_a_key_only_when_it_is_not_weaker`, `planner_revision_setting_ignores_the_hard_producer_setting`, `planner_revision_keys_leave_the_reading_digest_alone` and `planner_revision_ranking_relies_on_haiku_listed_before_sonnet`. `cargo test -p athena-data` passed 219 of 219 plus repo_config.

criteria_check.criterion: In crates/athena-data/src/config.rs, Models has optional planner_revision_model and planner_revision_effort. They are not derived from hard_producer_model or hard_producer_effort. Grep planning.rs for a diff showing no use of producer_setting or hard_producer_* in the planner path.
criteria_check.evidence: Models has two `Option<String>` fields with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`. `planner_revision_setting` reads only the two new keys, `producer_allowed` and `EFFORT_LEVELS`. The planning.rs diff calls `planner_revision_setting` and contains no `producer_setting` and no `hard_producer`. The config test `planner_revision_setting_ignores_the_hard_producer_setting` shows the result does not change with the hard_* values.

criteria_check.criterion: The owner can see the escalation. The planner line printed by planning_round, or the invocation record, shows the model used on the revision round. A test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs or in the core tests asserts it. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli` if drain.rs is changed.
criteria_check.evidence: The planner UI line is now `planner    {model} · {effort} · {wall}s · {cost}`. The core test asserts both the line and the invocation record for round 1 and for the revision round. drain.rs gains `planner_revision_takes_effect_in_the_repository_config`, which parses the repo's athena.toml. It asserts (sonnet, high) gives (sonnet, xhigh) and (haiku, high) gives (sonnet, xhigh). That test passed. The workspace run, which includes the full athena-cli suite, exited 0.

criteria_check.criterion: athena.toml has the new planner_revision_* entry under [models]. CHANGELOG.md has an entry that states the effective planner model and effort in this repo with and without the change, and what the keys do. docs/spec.toml, where it describes planning, mentions the revision setting.
criteria_check.evidence: athena.toml [models] has `planner_revision_model = "claude-sonnet-5-5"` and `planner_revision_effort = "xhigh"`, with comments that name the keys in backticks and say producer_allowed is weakest first. The drain.rs and config.rs tests parse the real athena.toml and passed.

open_issues: The model ranking is the order of `producer_allowed`, read weakest first. No code checks that order. It is stated in the doc comments and in athena.toml, and pinned by two tests: a table row with the list reversed, and a test that haiku is listed before sonnet in the repo config.
I could not read the background workspace test output, so I cite only its exit code 0 and the targeted runs. Athena's own check will confirm the full suite.
mistakes: My first attempt to edit config.rs used a here-document and was denied by the Bash hook. I redid the edits with the Edit tool. Nothing was written by the denied attempt.
learnings: The Athena Bash hook denies here-documents, pipes to tail or grep, `$?` and redirects, so each command must be one plain cargo or git call.

`repo_with_config` in run/tests.rs copies athena.toml minus [job_plan]. It now drops planner_revision_* lines, and the new `repo_with_config_and_models` inserts a test's own keys after the [models] header, so existing planning tests keep the unset behaviour.

`a_config_without_effort_keys_still_parses_with_the_default_effort` strips every line containing `_effort`, which also removes planner_revision_effort and its comment lines, so it still passes unchanged.
`an_unknown_effort_value_is_rejected_and_a_known_one_is_accepted` finds its line with `{key} = `, so the athena.toml comments name the keys in backticks with no ` = ` after them.
desires: A way to read a background task's output file from inside the working directory, so I can cite per-crate test counts for a long workspace run.
